title: Entropy-Based Detection of the Rest-to-Firing Transition in Morris–Lecar Dynamics Reconstructed from Sparse Voltage Data by Physics-Informed Neural Networks
content: Entropy measures are widely used to detect changes of dynamical regime, but their reliability when the signal must first be reconstructed from sparse, noisy recordings is rarely tested against an independently known transition. We studied the rest-to-firing transition of the class-I Morris–Lecar neuron, located by continuation at a saddle-node on invariant circle bifurcation (39.963 μA cm−2), and scored sample, permutation, weighted permutation, and spectral entropy by their localization error. Voltage traces were reduced to 50–5% of their samples, corrupted by noise, and reconstructed by a physics-informed neural network (PINN), cubic splines, and an ODE least-squares fit. On reference signals, permutation-type and spectral entropy located the transition to the grid resolution (0.012 μA cm−2), whereas sample entropy erred by 0.21 μA cm−2. Without noise, all reconstructions preserved these results down to 5% sparsity, and the PINN recovered the unobserved recovery variable with a median relative error of 0.027. With noise, residual fluctuations in resting windows reversed the entropy contrast at the transition while the localization error often stayed small; the effect was strongest for splines and absent for the ODE fit. Localization error must therefore be reported together with regime separability, and the quiescent threshold is part of the measurement protocol.
